correctness.rationale: PASS. The antipodal quotient F_2^n/<1> has 2^(n-1) characters indexed by even Walsh weights; the shortest-path distance is min(|x|,n-|x|). Its convolution Fourier transform has the indispensable 1/2 quotient-representative factor. Discrete integration by parts for the centered tent f(k) yields one or two central second-difference coefficients, giving the exact signed factorial spectrum and strictly positive constant row sum. Signs (-1)^a imply nonsingular inertia. The ratio |Lambda_{2(a+1)}|/|Lambda_{2a}| increases with a, so positive-mode magnitudes are log-convex; comparison of the admissible first and last positive levels yields all four stated cases of Q_n, including n=3, n odd, and n mod 4 boundaries. Independent direct Walsh sums from quotient representatives and Krawtchouk sums were compared in dimensions 3..10, all consistent; source CHECK.py expands to n=70 but finite tests alone do not prove arbitrary n. Positive centered eigenvalues for n>=4 imply negative-type failure and, by first-order Taylor expansion, loss of positive semidefiniteness of exp(-td) for sufficiently small t>0 only. No claim for all t.
